subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
subtype: Approach: pre-departure checklist and task decomposition [Action]
passage: I'm Minakshi, and a checklist saved me. Two weeks before leaving for college in another city, my father Chetan and I sat with a fresh notebook and wrote everything in groups: identity papers, admission letters, bank access, medicines, clothes, phone contacts. Each evening we ticked off one group. On day three we photocopied my papers and put the originals in a folder. On day six I set up online banking with him beside me and wrote the helpline number on a card. He kept saying, “Clothes come last, they're the easy part.” So the night before my train, I packed only what was left: clothes, a lamp, chargers. My bag was ready, and I slept. Looking back, breaking one huge word, moving, into small ticks made it feel possible.

qa.q: Which groups of things did Minakshi and Chetan write in the notebook?
qa.a: They wrote identity papers, admission letters, bank access, medicines, clothes and phone contacts.

qa.q: How did the list change Minakshi's feeling about moving?
qa.a: Minakshi felt calmer and more capable, since breaking moving into small ticks made it feel possible, and Minakshi slept the night before leaving.

qa.q: What could Minakshi do if some papers turned out to be missing at the last minute?
qa.a: Minakshi could ask the college office which originals are needed and how to get copies, because a checklist ticked early shows gaps before departure day.

qa.q: How might Chetan have felt during the two weeks of ticking off groups?
qa.a: Chetan probably felt reassured, since working on each group with Minakshi let him see the move was prepared and made it easier to let go.

grounding: A teen lists documents, papers, bank access, medicines, clothes and contacts, ticks them off over two weeks with a parent and packs essentials last.
